sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Kingship Theory**: Alauddin Khilji rejected the Ulema's interference in state affairs, famously stating, 'I do not know whether this is lawful or unlawful; whatever I think to be for the good of the state, I decree.'
• **Centralization**: Shifted power from the Turkish nobility (Chahalgani) to a loyal, professional bureaucracy and standing army.
• **Economic Control**: Implemented the most rigorous price control mechanism in medieval India to maintain a large standing army on limited revenue.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The 'Dagh' (branding of horses) and 'Chehra' (descriptive rolls of soldiers) were introduced to prevent corruption in the military.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix

Measurement of land (Masahat) and direct collection from peasants.
Standardized tax at 50% of produce; abolished intermediary rights of Khuts and Muqaddams.

Intelligence officers and secret spies respectively, ensuring the Sultan's absolute control over the administration.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Military Expansion**: Malik Kafur’s Deccan campaigns (Devagiri, Warangal, Dwarasamudra, Madurai) shifted the focus from territorial annexation to tribute extraction.
• **Anti-Rebellion Policy**: Four ordinances: confiscation of religious endowments (Waqf/Inam), strengthening spy network, banning liquor/gambling, and prohibiting social gatherings among nobles.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: The system was highly personality-dependent; it collapsed immediately after Alauddin's death due to the lack of institutional sustainability.
• **Solutions**: The Tughlaqs later adopted a more moderate revenue policy to stabilize the agrarian base.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'M-A-D-S' (Market, Arrears, Dagh, Spies).
• **Decoded Meaning**: M (Market Reforms), A (Arrears/Mustakhraj), D (Dagh/Chehra), S (Spies/Barids).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Alauddin's market reforms' as being applicable to the entire Sultanate. They were restricted primarily to Delhi and its immediate surroundings.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'State-led Mercantilism' to describe Alauddin's economic policies in the context of medieval statecraft.

keyTakeaways: Alauddin Khilji was the first Sultan to maintain a permanent standing army paid in cash.
The Khilji period represents the peak of centralized autocracy in the Delhi Sultanate.
Revenue reforms were aimed at maximizing state income to fund military expansion against Mongol threats.
